items.question: Up to what wind speed has starting and stopping the rotor been demonstrated, with the wind from any direction?
options: 30 kt (56 km/h)
40 kt (74 km/h)
50 kt (93 km/h)
items.explanation: Starting and stopping the rotor has been demonstrated for winds of 40 kt (74 km/h) from any direction, and 50 kt (93 km/h) with a headwind (forward center axis ±30°).

items.question: Hovering with wind from any direction has been demonstrated over the entire flight envelope up to what speed?
options: 10 kt (19 km/h)
17 kt (31 km/h)
23 kt (43 km/h)
30 kt (56 km/h)
items.explanation: Hovering with winds from any direction up to 17 kt (31 km/h) has been demonstrated over the entire flight envelope, although it is not to be taken as a limit.

items.question: What must the pilot check before takeoff, in HIGE at 5 ft and before initiating forward flight?
options: That the Ng can increase by at least 1% without exceeding the max. transient rating when the collective is pulled slightly
That the T4 margin is positive
That the VEMD FLI page shows GOOD
That fuel flow is within 5% of the planned value
items.explanation: In HIGE at 5 ft (1.5 m) and before initiating forward flight, the pilot pulls the collective pitch lever slightly to ensure the Ng can increase by at least 1%, without exceeding the max. transient rating.

items.question: The engine power check verifies which two margins?
options: Torque margin and t4 margin
Ng margin and NR margin
Fuel flow margin and oil pressure margin
Rotor speed margin and hydraulic pressure margin
items.explanation: The engine power check consists of checking the power margin (torque margin) and the t4 margin, either from VEMD data or manually recorded parameters.

items.question: Under what conditions must the VEMD engine power check be performed?
options: In a climb, at MTOP, with heating ON
In stabilized level flight at a power rating close to MCP, Hp ≤ 12000 ft, heating and demisting OFF
During autorotation, at any altitude
On the ground at idle, with the rotor brake applied
items.explanation: The VEMD engine power check must be performed in stabilized level flight at a power rating close to MCP, with Hp ≤ 12000 ft (3657 m) and the heating and demisting system OFF.

items.question: If the calculated t4 margin (before any correction) is greater than +35°C, what does this mean?
options: The result is acceptable without further calculation
The engine condition shall be considered unsatisfactory
The correction table no longer applies and must be ignored
The check must be repeated at a lower altitude only
items.explanation: The t4-margin-to-corrected-t4-margin correction only applies if the t4 margin (before correction) is less than +35°C. If the t4 margin is greater than +35°C, the engine state shall be considered unsatisfactory.

items.question: How is the corrected t4 margin calculated from the measured torque margin and t4 margin?
options: Corrected t4 margin = t4 margin − torque margin
Corrected t4 margin = t4 margin + (torque margin × correction factor)
Corrected t4 margin = torque margin × 2
Corrected t4 margin = t4 margin ÷ torque margin
items.explanation: The t4 margin correction equals the torque margin multiplied by a correction factor read from the Hp/OAT table; the corrected t4 margin is then the calculated t4 margin plus that correction.

items.question: In the height-velocity (HV) diagram, how is point A of the avoidance zone defined?
options: 100 ft height, variable airspeed
25 ft height, 40 kt constant airspeed
8 ft skid height at zero airspeed
Variable height at zero airspeed
items.explanation: Point A is the low hover point: 8 ft (2.5 m) skid height at zero airspeed.

items.question: In the height-velocity (HV) diagram, point B of the avoidance zone is defined by which fixed values?
options: 8 ft height, zero airspeed
25 ft height, 40 kt constant airspeed
100 ft height, variable airspeed
Variable height, zero airspeed
items.explanation: Point B is defined by a constant height of 25 ft (8 m) and a constant airspeed of 40 kt (74 km/h).

items.question: What glide performance is published for autorotation?
options: 0.54 NM per 1000 ft at IAS = 65 kt and NR ≥ 410 rpm
1.0 NM per 1000 ft at IAS = 80 kt and NR ≥ 386 rpm
0.25 NM per 1000 ft at IAS = 50 kt and NR ≥ 400 rpm
0.75 NM per 1000 ft at IAS = 65 kt and NR ≥ 420 rpm
items.explanation: The distance flown in autorotation is 0.54 NM per 1000 ft at an IAS of 65 kt and NR ≥ 410 rpm (1000 m per 300 m height at 120 km/h).
